title: The popularity of air fryers
paragraphs: For many time-poor, health-conscious people, the must-have kitchen gadget at the moment is an air fryer. From top chefs to humble students, many are singing the praises of the device that seems to be flying off the shelves at shops and online. One British department store reported sales increased by 400% in 2021. But are they really the best thing since sliced bread, or is the hype all just hot air?!

If you got one as a present, or bagged one in the sales, you'll already know the benefits. An air fryer avoids the need to deep-fry food in hot and often unhealthy oil. Instead, the food is cooked by having very hot air blown on it at high speed – it doesn't actually fry but bakes the food.

The technology sounds simple, and Dr Jakub Radzikowski, Culinary Education Designer at Imperial College London, told the BBC: "You could compare it to drying your hair with a hairdryer." The combination of a powerful fan and a smaller compartment makes the air fryer more efficient and reduces the time needed to pre-heat it. In addition, because the food is cooked in a basket, excess fat will drip to the bottom, so you don't have to eat it. And it's good to know air fryers use less energy than a conventional oven because of the shorter cooking times needed.

Some people may question how versatile they are and whether they can be used for cooking whole meals. But experts have prepared crispy sweet potato fries, chips, and chicken and fish, quickly and with good flavoursome results – cooked to perfection. Dr Jakub Radzikowski's favourite is chicken legs or thighs, which he says after 20 minutes gives you something that's "perfectly juicy inside" with a skin that is so crispy it "shatters like glass".

If this whets your appetite, remember that, because of the air fryer's size, there is a limit to the amount that can be cooked in them at one time. So your oven may still come in handy. But if you're on a budget or in a rush, it might be worth giving one a try and seeing what amazing meals you can serve up.

vocabulary.entry: **time-poor** /ˈtaɪm pʊə(r)/ adj. 时间紧张的；没空的
vocabulary.example: Many time-poor professionals rely on ready meals for dinner during the week.
vocabulary.translation: 许多时间紧张的职场人工作日晚餐都靠速食解决。

vocabulary.entry: **health-conscious** /ˈhelθ ˈkɒnʃəs/ adj. 注重健康的；有健康意识的
vocabulary.example: Health-conscious people usually avoid food with too much sugar and salt.
vocabulary.translation: 注重健康的人通常会避开高糖高盐的食物。

vocabulary.entry: **gadget** /ˈɡædʒɪt/ n. 小器具；小家电；小装置
vocabulary.example: This new kitchen gadget can peel and chop vegetables in seconds.
vocabulary.translation: 这款新的厨房小家电几秒内就能给蔬菜去皮切块。

vocabulary.entry: **air fryer** /eə(r) ˈfraɪə(r)/ n. 空气炸锅
vocabulary.example: An air fryer can make crispy chips with very little oil.
vocabulary.translation: 空气炸锅只用很少的油就能做出酥脆的薯条。

vocabulary.entry: **chef** /ʃef/ n. 主厨；厨师
vocabulary.example: The chef of this restaurant has won many international cooking awards.
vocabulary.translation: 这家餐厅的主厨斩获过多个国际烹饪奖项。

vocabulary.entry: **sing the praises of** /sɪŋ ðə ˈpreɪzɪz ɒv/ 盛赞；对……赞不绝口
vocabulary.example: Everyone who has used this product sings the praises of its convenience.
vocabulary.translation: 所有用过这款产品的人都对它的便捷性赞不绝口。

vocabulary.entry: **fly off the shelves** /flaɪ ɒf ðə ˈʃelvz/ 热销；被抢购一空
vocabulary.example: The new phone model is flying off the shelves just a week after its launch.
vocabulary.translation: 这款新手机上市仅一周就被抢购一空。

vocabulary.entry: **department store** /dɪˈpɑːtmənt stɔː(r)/ 百货公司；百货商店
vocabulary.example: You can buy almost everything you need in a big department store.
vocabulary.translation: 在大型百货公司里你几乎能买到所有需要的东西。

vocabulary.entry: **hype** /haɪp/ n. 大肆宣传；炒作；热度
vocabulary.example: There's a lot of hype around this new movie, but it's actually not that good.
vocabulary.translation: 这部新电影被炒得火热，但实际上并没有那么好看。

vocabulary.entry: **hot air** /hɒt eə(r)/ 空话；夸夸其谈；吹牛
vocabulary.example: What he said was just hot air – he never keeps his promises.
vocabulary.translation: 他说的不过是大话而已，他从来都不遵守承诺。

vocabulary.entry: **bag** /bæɡ/ v. 入手；抢购；捞到
vocabulary.example: I managed to bag a great jacket in the summer sale.
vocabulary.translation: 我在夏季大促里成功抢到了一件超棒的夹克。

vocabulary.entry: **deep-fry** /ˌdiːp ˈfraɪ/ v. 油炸；油汆
vocabulary.example: It's healthier to bake chicken instead of deep-fry it.
vocabulary.translation: 烤鸡肉比油炸鸡肉更健康。

vocabulary.entry: **culinary** /ˈkʌlɪnəri/ adj. 烹饪的；厨房的
vocabulary.example: She took a course to improve her culinary skills.
vocabulary.translation: 她报了一门课来提升自己的烹饪技巧。

vocabulary.entry: **hairdryer** /ˈheədraɪə(r)/ n. 吹风机
vocabulary.example: You should dry your wet hair with a hairdryer to avoid catching a cold.
vocabulary.translation: 你应该用吹风机吹干湿头发，避免感冒。

vocabulary.entry: **compartment** /kəmˈpɑːtmənt/ n. 腔体；隔层；隔间
vocabulary.example: The fridge has a special compartment for storing fruit and vegetables.
vocabulary.translation: 冰箱有一个专门的隔层用来存放水果蔬菜。

vocabulary.entry: **efficient** /ɪˈfɪʃnt/ adj. 高效的；效率高的
vocabulary.example: LED lights are more efficient than traditional bulbs and use less electricity.
vocabulary.translation: LED灯比传统灯泡效率更高，也更省电。

vocabulary.entry: **pre-heat** /ˌpriː ˈhiːt/ v. 预热
vocabulary.example: You need to pre-heat the oven to 180 degrees before baking the cake.
vocabulary.translation: 烤蛋糕前你需要把烤箱预热到180度。

vocabulary.entry: **excess** /ɪkˈses/ adj. 多余的；过量的
vocabulary.example: You should cut off excess fat from the meat before cooking it.
vocabulary.translation: 烹饪前你应该把肉上多余的脂肪切掉。

vocabulary.entry: **conventional** /kənˈvenʃənl/ adj. 传统的；常规的
vocabulary.example: Conventional farming methods use a lot of pesticides and fertilizers.
vocabulary.translation: 传统的耕作方式会使用大量的农药和化肥。

vocabulary.entry: **oven** /ˈʌvn/ n. 烤箱；烤炉
vocabulary.example: She put the bread in the oven to bake for 15 minutes.
vocabulary.translation: 她把面包放进烤箱烤15分钟。

vocabulary.entry: **versatile** /ˈvɜːsətaɪl/ adj. 多功能的；用途广泛的
vocabulary.example: A good chef's knife is the most versatile tool in the kitchen.
vocabulary.translation: 一把好的主厨刀是厨房里用途最广的工具。

vocabulary.entry: **crispy** /ˈkrɪspi/ adj. 酥脆的；爽脆的
vocabulary.example: The fried chicken has a crispy skin and tender meat inside.
vocabulary.translation: 这炸鸡外皮酥脆，内里肉质鲜嫩。

vocabulary.entry: **flavoursome** /ˈfleɪvəsəm/ adj. 味道浓郁的；可口的
vocabulary.example: Slow cooking makes the meat tender and flavoursome.
vocabulary.translation: 慢炖能让肉质软烂，味道浓郁。

vocabulary.entry: **thigh** /θaɪ/ n. （禽的）大腿；大腿
vocabulary.example: Chicken thigh is more juicy and flavourful than chicken breast.
vocabulary.translation: 鸡大腿比鸡胸肉更多汁、更入味。

vocabulary.entry: **juicy** /ˈdʒuːsi/ adj. 多汁的；汁水充盈的
vocabulary.example: The steak was perfectly cooked, tender and juicy.
vocabulary.translation: 这块牛排煎得恰到好处，鲜嫩多汁。

vocabulary.entry: **shatter** /ˈʃætə(r)/ v. 碎裂；粉碎；破碎
vocabulary.example: The glass will shatter if you drop it on the hard floor.
vocabulary.translation: 如果你把玻璃杯掉在坚硬的地板上，它会摔得粉碎。

vocabulary.entry: **whet your appetite** /wet jɔː(r) ˈæpɪtaɪt/ 勾起食欲；激起兴趣
vocabulary.example: The smell of freshly baked bread will whet your appetite.
vocabulary.translation: 新鲜出炉的面包的香气会勾起你的食欲。

vocabulary.entry: **come in handy** /kʌm ɪn ˈhændi/ 派上用场；有用处
vocabulary.example: Always keep a first-aid kit in your car – it might come in handy.
vocabulary.translation: 车里要常备急救箱，说不定什么时候就能派上用场。

vocabulary.entry: **on a budget** /ɒn ə ˈbʌdʒɪt/ 预算有限；节省开支
vocabulary.example: We're on a budget this month, so we won't eat out too much.
vocabulary.translation: 我们这个月预算有限，所以不会经常出去吃饭。

vocabulary.entry: **serve up** /sɜːv ʌp/ 端上（饭菜）；做出（美食）
vocabulary.example: She can serve up a delicious meal in less than 30 minutes.
vocabulary.translation: 她能在不到30分钟里做出一顿美味的饭菜。

sentences.english: For many time-poor, health-conscious people, the must-have kitchen gadget at the moment is an air fryer.
sentences.chinese: 对于许多时间紧张、注重健康的人来说，当下厨房必备的小家电就是空气炸锅。

sentences.english: From top chefs to humble students, many are singing the praises of the device that seems to be flying off the shelves at shops and online.
sentences.chinese: 从顶级大厨到普通学生，许多人都对这款设备赞不绝口，它在线上线下的商店里都卖得异常火爆。

sentences.english: One British department store reported sales increased by 400% in 2021.
sentences.chinese: 英国一家百货公司报告称，2021年空气炸锅的销量涨幅高达400%。

sentences.english: But are they really the best thing since sliced bread, or is the hype all just hot air?!
sentences.chinese: 但它们真的是继切片面包之后最棒的发明吗？还是说这场热度不过是夸夸其谈？

sentences.english: If you got one as a present, or bagged one in the sales, you'll already know the benefits.
sentences.chinese: 如果你收到过一台空气炸锅作为礼物，或是在促销时入手了一台，那你一定已经知道它的好处。

sentences.english: An air fryer avoids the need to deep-fry food in hot and often unhealthy oil.
sentences.chinese: 空气炸锅无需用滚烫且往往不健康的油来油炸食物。

sentences.english: Instead, the food is cooked by having very hot air blown on it at high speed – it doesn't actually fry but bakes the food.
sentences.chinese: 相反，它是通过高速吹送热风来烹制食物——它实际上并非油炸，而是烘烤食物。

sentences.english: The technology sounds simple, and Dr Jakub Radzikowski, Culinary Education Designer at Imperial College London, told the BBC: "You could compare it to drying your hair with a hairdryer."
sentences.chinese: 这项技术听起来十分简单，伦敦帝国理工学院的烹饪教育设计师雅各布·拉齐科夫斯基博士在接受BBC采访时表示：“你可以把它比作用吹风机吹头发。”

sentences.english: The combination of a powerful fan and a smaller compartment makes the air fryer more efficient and reduces the time needed to pre-heat it.
sentences.chinese: 强劲的风扇和更小的腔体相结合，让空气炸锅的效率更高，还缩短了预热所需的时间。

sentences.english: In addition, because the food is cooked in a basket, excess fat will drip to the bottom, so you don't have to eat it.
sentences.chinese: 此外，由于食物是放在炸篮中烹制的，多余的油脂会滴落到容器底部，你也就不会摄入这些油脂了。

sentences.english: And it's good to know air fryers use less energy than a conventional oven because of the shorter cooking times needed.
sentences.chinese: 而且值得一提的是，由于烹制时间更短，空气炸锅比传统烤箱更省电。

sentences.english: Some people may question how versatile they are and whether they can be used for cooking whole meals.
sentences.chinese: 有些人可能会质疑它们的用途是否广泛，能不能用来做一整顿饭。

sentences.english: But experts have prepared crispy sweet potato fries, chips, and chicken and fish, quickly and with good flavoursome results – cooked to perfection.
sentences.chinese: 但专家们已经用空气炸锅快速做出了酥脆的甜薯条、炸薯块、鸡肉和鱼肉，成品味道上佳，火候恰到好处。

sentences.english: Dr Jakub Radzikowski's favourite is chicken legs or thighs, which he says after 20 minutes gives you something that's "perfectly juicy inside" with a skin that is so crispy it "shatters like glass".
sentences.chinese: 雅各布·拉齐科夫斯基博士最爱的是用它做鸡腿或鸡大腿，他说，20分钟后，就能得到一份“内里汁水充盈”、外皮酥脆到“像玻璃一样一碰就碎”的成品。

sentences.english: If this whets your appetite, remember that, because of the air fryer's size, there is a limit to the amount that can be cooked in them at one time.
sentences.chinese: 如果这让你心动了，要记住，受限于空气炸锅的尺寸，它一次能烹制的食物量是有限的。

sentences.english: So your oven may still come in handy.
sentences.chinese: 所以你的烤箱可能还是能派上用场。

sentences.english: But if you're on a budget or in a rush, it might be worth giving one a try and seeing what amazing meals you can serve up.
sentences.chinese: 但如果你预算有限，或是时间紧张，不妨试试空气炸锅，看看能做出多少惊艳的美食。
